evidence: Cic. Fam. 14.4.4: nihil est quod tē moveat
terms.comment: With a genitive, “nothing (of)”: nihil novī, nothing new. A second-declension adjective goes into the genitive (nihil malī, nothing bad); a third-declension one agrees (nihil ūtile, nothing useful). “Nothing but” is nihil nisi or nihil aliud nisi (Cic. Amic. 20). “And nothing” is nec quicquam (see anything). Nihil nōn, “nothing not”, is everything (Lewis & Short).

terms.register: vōx plērumque poētica et cōmica: Plaut., Hor.; also post-Augustan prose (Lewis & Short)
evidence: Hor. S. 1.9.19: nīl habeō quod agam
Cic. Fin. 2.43: inter optimē valēre et gravissimē aegrōtāre nihil prōrsus interesse (Lewis & Short s.v. inter)

terms.gloss: nothing (in set phrases: ex nihilō, ad nihilum, prō nihilō, nihilī)
evidence: Cic. Div. 2.37: erit aliquid, quod aut ex nihilō oriātur, aut in nihilum subitō occidat (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fat. 18: ut dē nihilō quippiam fīat (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: hoc igitur habēbis, novī nihil. quid ergō opus erat epistulā?
phrases.english: so there you have it: nothing new. Then why write a letter at all?

phrases.latin: jam diū ignōrō quid agās; nihil enim scrībis
phrases.english: for a long time now I haven’t known how you are, since you write nothing

phrases.latin: nīl habeō quod agam et nōn sum piger: ūsque sequar tē
phrases.english: I’ve nothing to do and I’m not lazy: I’ll follow you all the way
there is nothing to upset you

phrases.latin: est enim amīcitia nihil aliud nisi omnium dīvīnārum hūmānārumque rērum cum benevolentiā et cāritāte cōnsēnsiō
phrases.english: for friendship is nothing but agreement in all things divine and human, with goodwill and affection

phrases.latin: Nihil vērō ūtile, quod nōn idem honestum
phrases.english: nothing is useful that is not also honourable

phrases.latin: nihil umquam malī huic agrō fēcī
phrases.english: I never did this field any harm
I have nothing ready but myself

phrases.latin: erit aliquid, quod aut ex nihilō oriātur, aut in nihilum subitō occidat
phrases.english: there will be something that either arises out of nothing or suddenly falls away into nothing
